sections.content:
The green bar changed! Looking at the diff:
- Row 9: cols 30-32 changed from 'N' (light green) to 'B' (black) - the right part of the green bar disappeared
- Row 10: col 28 changed from 'N' to 'r' (red), col 30-32 changed from 'N'/'r' to 'B'
- Row 11: cols 30-32 changed from 'N' to 'B'
So the green bar (which was horizontal at rows 9-11, cols 28-32) has been shortened from the right side. The red dot that was at (10, 31) disappeared (became black), and a new red dot appeared at (10, 28).
This is similar to the yellow bar mechanism - clicking on the green U-shape shrunk the green bar and moved the red dot.
Now I understand the pattern:
- Each colored bar has a red dot inside it
- Each bar has a corresponding container with U-shapes of the same color
- Clicking on a U-shape toggles the bar between expanded and contracted states
- The two U-shapes in each container toggle in opposite directions
Let me check the current state of the green bar and try clicking the second green U-shape to see if it reverses the change.

# Check current green bar state
seg = current_frame.segmentation

    if n['color'] in ['N', 'r'] and n['pixels'] <= 20:
        b = n['boundary']
        rows = [p[0] for p in b]
        cols = [p[1] for p in b]
        print(f"  Node {n['id']}: color={n['color']}, pixels={n['pixels']}, bbox=({min(rows)},{min(cols)})-({max(rows)},{max(cols)})")

# Now click on the second green U-shape (node 14 at rows 20-22, cols 44-46)
result = action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 21, 'col': 45}])

# Check diff

after_ascii = last_transition.after_frame.ascii
before_lines = before_ascii.split('\n')
after_lines = after_ascii.split('\n')

diffs = []
for i, (bl, al) in enumerate(zip(before_lines, after_lines)):
    for j, (bc, ac) in enumerate(zip(bl, al)):
        if bc != ac:
            diffs.append((i, j, bc, ac))

print(f"\nAfter clicking green U-shape 2:")
print(f"Total cells changed: {len(diffs)}")
from collections import defaultdict
by_row = defaultdict(list)
for r, c, bc, ac in diffs:
    by_row[r].append((c, bc, ac))
for r in sorted(by_row.keys()):
    print(f"  Row {r}: {by_row[r]}")
</parameter>
</function>
